subject: Question for Shiny data file saving and loading

messages.author: 65c143e827bc7dfe
messages.subject: Question for Shiny data file saving and loading
parts:
Hi all,
I have built an application that has an reactive input, and when the input changes, it calls a customized function X(), in which it saves a model to a RData file. 
My question is, if I have two different clients that visit my app from their machine, when they change the input, will that RData file be stored/loaded on/from server side or locally? 
If server side, then will it cause synchronizing issues? If client side, then what path should I define?

Here's some code for reference:

server <- function(input,output,session){
  model <- reactive({
    modelRes<-NA
    
      setProgress(message = "Updating Model...")

      #Model is saved in "ValueMatrix.RData" in this function TopicModelTrain(), e.g., save(model, file = "ValueMatrix.RData")
      TopicModelTrain(isolate({input$sparsity}),isolate({input$TFIDFfilterLevel}),0.9,TRUE,input$topicNum,isolate({input$newdatatrain}),testingData,20,10)  

      load("ValueMatrix.RData")

        ......

    return(modelRes)
  })
  ......
}

Appreciate your help!

Thank you for your reply. The reason is that different user might use different data to retrain the model, and at first I wrote the function for local use and ended up with saving it to a file. That's why I was thinking of synchronization when it comes to server and client side.
So it is supposed to save the file to server? Which means it is better to return all variables from TopicModelTrain() directly, instead of save them to a file? 

Thanks.

messages.subject: Re: Question for Shiny data file saving and loading
parts:
Also, another important reason is that, the training data might or might not be changed, which means user could at some point train a model with new data, or still use the previous model if no new data is coming. 
We do not want to go through the training process every new session, because when original dataset is large, it might take a long time, and if no new data within a while, we could reuse the model if save to a file.
